note:
Malcolm, 2026-08-25: 'a very close up of the top of the open jar (same product with light blue cream) showing the cream very close up'.

WHAT IS THERE NOW is the whole jar — Copper Peptide Advanced Night Repair, lid propped beside it, label fully legible, shot at product-hero distance and cropped to 4:3 out of the existing library (assets/faq-final/faq-ingredients-safety.png). It sells the pack. It does not show the formulation, which is what an Ingredients & Safety block is about.

SO THE SUBJECT CHANGES FROM THE PACK TO THE CONTENTS. The camera moves in until the mouth of the jar is wider than the picture, and the pale blue cream itself becomes the whole photograph.

NO REFERENCE IMAGE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. At this magnification not one character of the label is in frame, so there is nothing for a reference to lock. Sending the product reference anyway would do the opposite of what it looks like it does: every engine that takes an edit reference pulls the framing back toward the reference's own distance, which is exactly the product-hero shot being replaced, and the ones that restage hardest would put the label back in and misspell it — PDRN came back as PORN once already. The jar is described instead, and every form of lettering is barred outright. That also lets FLUX.2 run, which is barred from reference shots by the script.

THE FRAME IS STATED AS AN EDGE CONDITION, not as a background — the same correction that fixed the Skincare & Routine block earlier today. Cream and glass reach all four edges and there is no backdrop anywhere to be described, which is the only reliable way to stop an engine putting a black bar under the white title.

THE CREAM IS SPECIFIED, NOT NAMED. 'Cream in a jar' comes back white on every engine; the formulation is opaque soft light blue #A6C4E0, satin rather than glossy, thick enough to hold a peak. Colour, finish and body are all stated, and white is barred in the negatives.

GEOMETRY IS MEASURED, NOT DESCRIBED. 'Very close up' means nothing to six different engines, so the closeness is pinned to the frame: the mouth is wider than the picture, the rim band is about one fifth of the picture height, and the whorl of the swirl is about a third of the picture width.

BRIGHT BLOCK. Like the shot it replaces this is a pale frame, so it keeps the `bright` flag in the IMAGES map — the steeper per-block scrim ramp that takes a pale picture's title from about 4:1 to about 11:1. Contrast is bought from the scrim so the photograph never has to be composed around the type.

slots.title: Ingredients & Safety — into the open jar, the cream is the whole picture
slots.prompt: Macro product photograph, landscape format, looking down into the open mouth of a cosmetic cream jar from a steep angle a little above and in front of the rim. The camera is close enough that the mouth of the jar is wider than the picture: the cream and the glass fill the frame corner to corner, and no background, no backdrop, no table, no surface and no empty space is visible anywhere in the picture, least of all along the top edge. Running left to right across the upper part of the frame, curving gently downward at each end as a wide circle does when it is cropped, is the far wall of the jar seen from inside: a thick smooth wall of frosted pale ice-blue glass, its polished top rim reading as a soft bright line, and just below that rim two shallow screw threads winding round the inside of the neck. That band of glass takes up about one fifth of the picture's height and the rest of the picture, all the way to the left, right and bottom edges, is cream. The cream is opaque and a soft light blue, hex #A6C4E0, clearly tinted and never white — a satin finish that returns a soft broad sheen rather than a wet gloss. It is thick and holds its shape: the surface is smooth and freshly filled, and at the centre it rises into one soft swirled peak where the filling nozzle lifted away, the whorl of that swirl about a third of the picture's width, its ridges soft-edged and rounded rather than sharp. Where the cream meets the glass it curves up the inside wall in a gentle meniscus and sits a little translucent at that edge, a shade paler where the light passes through it. Across the rest of the surface the texture is very fine: minute soft undulations and a scatter of tiny pinhead air bubbles just under the sheen, the kind of detail only visible this close. One large soft key from the upper left rakes across the swirl so the peak throws a soft shadow to the lower right and the ridges read as form, with one dim cool fill on the shadow side so the pale blue keeps its colour instead of blowing out to white. 100mm macro at f8, the swirl and the surface around it sharp, the far rim falling gently soft, fine film grain, cool neutral colour, quiet and expensive.
